Name: Espresso & Machine Masterclass at La Marzocco
Master_Aurora_Insights: La Marzocco opens its Florence factory and training centre to coffee enthusiasts for a full-day immersion in espresso. Known for hand-built machines used in specialty cafés worldwide, the company begins with a guided walk along the assembly line to see how each unit is constructed. The session then moves to the training bar for hands-on work. Under the instruction of professional baristas, you learn grinding, dosing and extraction; practice steaming milk and pouring latte art; and calibrate grinders and machines for consistent results.

Name: After-Hours Chef’s Table at Le Louis XV
Master_Aurora_Insights: After the last guests depart, Le Louis XV - Alain Ducasse at the Hôtel de Paris Monte‑Carlo opens privately for an after-hours chef’s table in Monaco. The three‑Michelin‑star team prepares an extended tasting centered on Riviera produce, paced to your table and the chef’s live decisions. Each course is paired by the sommelier team with selections drawn from the Hôtel de Paris cellar.

Name: Champagne Library Dinner at Ruinart
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Deep beneath Reims, dinner unfolds in Ruinart’s chalk crayères, part of the UNESCO-listed Champagne cellars that thread under the city. You and your guests descend by candlelight to a table set among centuries-old bottles. A maison historian outlines the cellar’s history and the practice of dégorgement, while a chef serves a multi-course menu calibrated to the house’s library champagnes.  

Comparable dinners can be arranged at houses such as Krug, Veuve Clicquot, or Salon, each with its own cellar stories and cuvées.

Name: Pagani Atelier Tour and Test Track Driving
Master_Aurora_Insights: A full-day immersion at Pagani’s atelier near Modena, in Italy’s Motor Valley, moving from workshop floor to test track. The program opens with an intimate design walkthrough centered on Horacio Pagani’s philosophy, followed by time with the artisans who sculpt each carbon‑fibre panel for the brand’s hand‑built hypercars. You then take to a test track for driving laps with guidance from an experienced coach.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Free cancellation is possible within 2 working days from the day of your tour. In case of a later cancellation or in case of no-show, paid tickets will not be refunded. In case of refund due, Modenatur will keep € 5 per ticket to cover booking fees and refund management.

Name: Maserati Modena Factory Tour and Track Drive
Master_Aurora_Insights: A factory and track program inside Maserati’s Officine in Modena, within Emilia‑Romagna’s Motor Valley. A private guide leads a behind‑the‑scenes tour through heritage halls and live production, showing how the trident marque is built. The day moves to a closed circuit, where a racing instructor rides alongside as you take the wheel of one of Maserati’s newest models for structured laps focused on car control and pace.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: After the tickets have been purchased, visitors can cancel their factory tour up to 7 days before the tour date and receive a full refund except for a €5 per ticket booking handling fee. For cancellations within 7 days, refunds will not be possible.

Name: Automobili Lamborghini Sant’Agata Bolognese Factory Tour and Track Drive
Master_Aurora_Insights: A factory tour and private‑circuit driving day at Automobili Lamborghini in Sant’Agata Bolognese, Emilia‑Romagna. Behind the doors of the headquarters, you observe the build of the marque’s V10 and V12 models: artisan carbon‑fibre layups and engines running at full voice. After the tour, a racing instructor leads lapping sessions on a private track to explore the Huracán (V10) or Aventador (V12).

Name: McLaren Technology Centre Tour and Track Drive
Master_Aurora_Insights: Inside the Norman Foster–designed McLaren Technology Centre in Woking, the day opens with a survey of championship cars and a look at cutting‑edge production. It then moves to a private circuit, where a McLaren instructor refines line and pace through each corner and straight as you sample a 720S or Artura.

Name: Aston Martin Gaydon Factory Tour and Track Drive
Master_Aurora_Insights:
A day inside Aston Martin’s Gaydon headquarters in Warwickshire, moving from the design studio to the production line before driving a DB11 or Vantage on the site’s private handling circuit. A seasoned instructor rides alongside, coaching your turn‑in and exit lines and noting the car’s composure and power.
The itinerary includes time on the factory floor to watch craftspeople hand‑stitch leather and work on wood veneers.

Name: Bentley Crewe Factory Tour and Track Drive
Master_Aurora_Insights: A behind-the-scenes and track program at Bentley’s Crewe factory in Cheshire. The visit moves through workshops dedicated to wood, leather and metalwork, showing the hand-finished details of production. After the factory tour, a professional driver leads a session on a private proving ground, with you taking the wheel of a Continental or a Flying Spur to understand the balance between power and ride comfort.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: In the unlikely event that you should need to cancel this booking, please notify our office at your earliest convenience. Cancellations made within 48 hours will be non-refundable. Should Bentley Experience, for reasons beyond its control, need to cancel a booking, an alternative date will be offered where possible. Bentley Experience cannot accept liability for any loss, financial or otherwise, under such circumstances.

Name: Bugatti Molsheim Factory Tour and Chiron Track Drive
Master_Aurora_Insights: A factory track day at Bugatti’s Molsheim estate, centered on Château Saint‑Jean, moves from heritage to performance. The programme begins inside the château with an introduction to the marque’s history, then goes behind the scenes in the atelier, where artisans assemble every W16 engine by hand. You then pilot a Chiron on a private track with expert coaching, with instruction and pacing tailored to driving goals.

Name: Silverstone Circuit Private Track Day
Master_Aurora_Insights: Silverstone Circuit, the home of British motorsport and host of the Formula 1 British Grand Prix, becomes your private circuit for the day. The programme begins with a technical briefing before you take a selection of supercars onto the high‑speed layout with guidance from seasoned instructors. Laps work through signature sections, 'Maggots, Becketts and the run to Club', with coaching tailored to pace and line. Between sessions, a hospitality lounge above the pits serves gourmet refreshments and displays real‑time telemetry from the cars.

Name: McLaren Technology Centre F1 Simulator Session
Master_Aurora_Insights:
A private session inside the simulator suite at the McLaren Technology Centre, the Norman Foster–designed campus for McLaren’s Formula 1 operation in Woking. You take the seat in a professional simulator typically reserved for F1 development drivers. Race engineers configure the car and circuit to your brief, then refine the setup stint by stint, reviewing telemetry between runs while drinks and snacks are on hand. 

Comparable formats are available at Aston Martin Racing HQ, at Red Bull Racing in Milton Keynes, and at boutique venues such as The Grid London or the Monaco GP Club Simulator. Each centers on realistic race preparation: circuit selection, car setup, and data-led feedback.

Name: Rimac Nevera Test Track Drive and Factory Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights:
A full-day immersion at Rimac’s Croatian campus outside Zagreb with track time in the brand’s electric hypercar program. The visit begins inside the factory, where engineers introduce proprietary battery systems and lightweight materials before you move to a secluded test track for guided runs with company test drivers. 
On track, you test the Rimac C_Two,_ now produced as the Nevera, focusing on instant torque and near‑silent power delivery. Midday, lunch features regional cuisine and open conversation with Rimac engineers about development and performance.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: For a full refund, you must cancel at least 24 hours before the experience’s start time. If you cancel less than 24 hours before the experience’s start time, the amount you paid will not be refunded. Any changes made less than 24 hours before the experience’s start time will not be accepted. This experience requires a minimum number of travelers. If it’s canceled because the minimum isn’t met, you’ll be offered a different date/experience or a full refund.

Name: Dubai Autodrome Private Supercar Track Day
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private day on the Dubai Autodrome circuit set in the desert. Following a professional briefing, you lap its technical layout in a roster of supercars, moving through tight chicanes and long straights with coaching to sharpen technique. Between sessions, an air‑conditioned suite serves as a base for refreshments and analysis.
Master_Cancellation_Policy:
No refunds, cancellations or re-scheduling will be provided for online or over-the-counter bookings once made.
We reserve the right to cancel an experience due to adverse weather conditions that may affect your safety. You will be entitled to use an alternative experience session no more than three months after the initial cancelled experience.
No refunds, credits or re-scheduling will be provided for guests not arriving on the correct day or time of the booking.
Dubai Kartdrome reserve the right to cancel an activity due to any governmental directive provided.

Name: Autódromo Internacional do Algarve Private Track Day
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private track day at Autódromo Internacional do Algarve (Portimão), the undulating circuit in Portugal that has hosted Formula 1 and MotoGP. The day begins with a morning briefing before an expert coach takes you section by section, adapting each part of the lap to your skill. Driving sessions rotate through a fleet of supercars, working across the roller‑coaster elevation changes and cambered turns that define the layout. Between runs, breaks unfold in a private suite with Algarve cuisine and structured review of driving data.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: In case of cancellation, Parkalgar is not obliged to refund the value of the ticket. Parkalgar will not refund the acquisition of experience vouchers if the user cannot take part in the experience due to non-compliance with the participation conditions. Vouchers must be used within the indicated period of use; Parkalgar will not refund expired vouchers. Right of withdrawal is non-applicable for tickets.

Name: Ferrari Tailor Made Design Session in Maranello
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private design session inside Ferrari’s Tailor Made atelier in Maranello. Working with a personal designer, you select materials, colours and finishes for a future Prancing Horse. The process is tactile: rare fabrics and heritage palettes laid out for inspection while atelier artisans build a full mock‑up rendering in real time. Between decisions, espresso is served and the team shares anecdotes drawn from Ferrari’s archives. The session runs over several hours and concludes with a detailed design specification, timed to align with the marque’s build cycles.

Name: Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari Private Supercar Driving
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private driving day at the Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari in Imola, the Formula 1 circuit where Ayrton Senna raced. Under the guidance of a racing coach, you take the wheel of a curated fleet of supercars. The program opens with a technical briefing, then on‑track sessions that work through the circuit’s signature corners: 'Tamburello and Rivazza', with instruction on lines, braking, and pace. Telemetry analysis follows each run, translating lap data into adjustments for the next session.  Between stints, a private paddock suite serves Emilia‑Romagna cuisine.

Name: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps Private Track Driving Day
Master_Aurora_Insights:
A full-day private driving program at Circuit de Spa‑Francorchamps, the 7.004 km Grand Prix circuit set in Belgium’s Ardennes. After a detailed technical briefing, you take to the track in a choice of supercars with a professional instructor in the passenger seat, adjusting each lap to your pace and skill. 

The day runs from hospitality suites overlooking Eau Rouge, used for debriefs and service between sessions, with gourmet meals served in-suite. Track time is reserved in advance to ensure dedicated private running. With a long lap, significant elevation through the Eau Rouge–Raidillon sequence, and extended high‑speed sections, the schedule emphasizes progressive, coached pacing.

Name: Autodromo Internazionale del Mugello Track Day with Coaching
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private circuit day at the Autodromo Internazionale del Mugello in Tuscany, home to MotoGP’s Italian Grand Prix. The program begins with a bespoke orientation, then moves into repeated stints on track in modern supercars. A professional driver provides line‑by‑line feedback on each section of the circuit. Between runs, you step into a trackside suite to review performance data and eat Tuscan dishes.

Cancellation between 4 and 6 weeks (42 to 28 days) before the event: 30% of the total payment charged.

Name: Ascari Race Resort Private Track Day
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private track day at Ascari Race Resort in the hills of Andalusia. The circuit sits among olive groves with mountain views. You start with one-to-one coaching from a professional instructor, then run supercars through a 26‑corner layout inspired by legendary circuits. Sessions break in the clubhouse, where tapas and wine are served between stints.

Name: Koenigsegg Ängelholm Design Session and Production Line Visit
Master_Aurora_Insights: A guided design session inside Koenigsegg’s studio in Ängelholm, the Swedish hypercar marque’s headquarters on a former Swedish Air Force base. You work with the design team to define colours, interior textures and trim, and specify aerodynamic elements, reviewing carbon-fibre weaves, metals and finishes at the bench. The visit extends onto the “Ghost Squadron” production line, Koenigsegg’s factory floor, observing monocoques, powertrains and bodywork at close range.  The session concludes with personalised renderings of your specification and a concise view of the marque’s approach to materials and performance.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Lamborghini Ad Personam Configuration Session
Master_Aurora_Insights: A personalization session inside Lamborghini’s Ad Personam studio at the marque’s Sant’Agata Bolognese headquarters. Design consultants work with you to translate preferences into leather, Alcantara, and paint, specifying colours and trims across the car. Digital renderings display each decision as the configuration takes shape. The visit includes a guided walk through the production line and access to a private espresso bar within the studio.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Roland Garros Private Tennis Lesson
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private training session on the red clay at Roland Garros, home of the French Open in Paris. You work one-to-one with an ex-professional who refines footwork and stroke mechanics through structured drills. The stadium is closed for the session, and an on-court photographer documents each rally.  After play, a courtside aperitivo is served. The day concludes in a private lounge with champagne and gourmet bites.

Name: Rimac Hypercar Design Session
Master_Aurora_Insights: A working session inside Rimac’s Bespoke Lab in Croatia, focused on the development of electric hypercars from the company known for the all-electric Nevera and the Bugatti Rimac joint venture. You sit with Rimac engineers to define materials, colours, and performance parameters specific to your vehicle. Interactive displays detail battery technology and present sustainable interior fabrics, while studio designers translate selections into live 3D renders. A curated tasting of Croatian delicacies punctuates the design process.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Monteblanco Circuit Private Track Day
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private driving day on Spain’s Monteblanco circuit with uninterrupted track time and a rotation of supercars, guided by expert instructors. The program opens with a briefing and runs through multiple on-track sessions, paced to build familiarity and speed. Between runs, Andalusian cuisine is served in a private lounge.

Name: Circuit Paul Ricard Private Track Day
Master_Aurora_Insights: At Circuit Paul Ricard on the Le Castellet plateau in Provence, a private day on track centers on the circuit’s long straights and technical turns. Engineers brief you before driving a stable of McLaren, Aston Martin, or Ferrari models, with a racing coach on hand to hone technique. Between sessions, a private suite with panoramic views serves Provençal cuisine and a quiet place to reset.

Name: Pagani Atelier Hypercar Configuration Session
Master_Aurora_Insights: Inside Pagani’s light‑filled atelier in San Cesario sul Panaro, Modena’s Motor Valley, the marque’s craftsmen host a hypercar design session. You sit with master artisans to specify carbon‑fiber weaves, leather tones, and metal finishes for a bespoke build. A physical model preview and mocked‑up renderings map every contour and surface before any decision is locked. Conversations with the team that realises Horacio Pagani’s designs run alongside the process, with Italian espresso at hand. The session concludes with a take‑home portfolio, material references, render images, and specifications, documenting the configuration.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Club des Pyramides Private Tennis Lesson
Master_Aurora_Insights: Just outside Paris, Club des Pyramides opens a private court for a one-to-one lesson led by a seasoned professional. Set within parkland grounds, the session focuses on technique and tactics, moving through targeted drills and situational play. You train while a photographer documents the day, building a visual record of the work on court. After play, a French aperitif is served in the clubhouse.

Name: Yas Marina Circuit Grand Prix Private Track Hire
Master_Aurora_Insights:
A full‑day private hire of Yas Marina Circuit in Abu Dhabi, running on the Grand Prix layout that hosts the Formula 1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. Track time unfolds under the floodlights, with sessions spanning daylight into evening.

You rotate through a stable of supercars on the GP circuit, coached by professional drivers. Between runs, gourmet dining is served in air‑conditioned suites for recovery and briefing.

Name: McLaren Special Operations Design Consultation, Factory and Gallery Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: Inside McLaren Special Operations in Woking, the marque’s bespoke division, you explore novel materials and bespoke aerodynamics for a future McLaren build. An MSO designer works through your brief in real time, sketching concepts while explaining advanced composites and finishes. Between design sessions, the program moves onto the factory floor with a guided walk through the production hall and a visit to the heritage car gallery on McLaren’s Woking campus. Following the visit, you receive a full specification document and a rendering that capture the agreed direction.

Name: Aston Martin Q Division Car Design Consultation
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private design appointment inside Aston Martin’s Q Division at the brand’s Gaydon headquarters in Warwickshire. You work with the design team to co‑create a DBX, Vantage, or Valhalla, selecting from extensive personalization options. Rare veneers, embroidery patterns, and paint swatches are presented over afternoon tea. A digital configurator allows real‑time iterations, while clay modelling is used to refine surfaces and proportions. The session concludes with a comprehensive design dossier detailing specifications, finishes, and elements.

Name: Porsche Leipzig Factory Tour and Track Driving
Master_Aurora_Insights: A full-day program inside Porsche’s Leipzig experience centre linking a behind-the-scenes factory visit with coached driving on the on-site test circuit. The day opens with an insider tour of the production lines before you take the wheel of a 911 or Taycan for instructor-led laps focused on precision handling. Sessions are structured with breaks: a chef’s table lunch served in a dining space overlooking the track, and time to browse a display of heritage race cars.
Master_Cancellation_Policy:
The participant can withdraw from the booking at any time before the start of the booked experience offer. Cancellation fees are:
• From the 15th calendar day before the programme date: 50% of the offer price.
• From the 3rd calendar day before the programme date or in case of no-show: 100% of the offer price.

Name: Monte-Carlo Country Club Clay-Court Tennis Session
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private clay-court session at Monte‑Carlo Country Club, set on the cliffs above the Mediterranean. A seasoned coach leads drills and point play with adjustments to technique and footwork as sea air moves across the baseline. A photographer documents the training throughout, building a visual record of the session. Aperitivo follows on a terrace with panoramic coastal views.

Name: Novak Djokovic Foundation Charity Match and Reception
Master_Aurora_Insights: A charity match under the auspices of the Novak Djokovic Foundation places you on court with Novak Djokovic in support of his philanthropic work. Professional production captures the on‑court action. A post‑match reception follows with signed merchandise and time for conversation with Djokovic. Scheduling is coordinated around his tournament and travel calendar.

Name: Bugatti Molsheim Sur Mesure Chiron Configuration Session
Master_Aurora_Insights: A design session inside Bugatti’s Sur Mesure studio at the marque’s Molsheim campus in Alsace. The visit begins with a guided look at Molsheim’s history before moving into a working atelier where you collaborate with Bugatti designers to configure a bespoke Chiron. Paints, leather trims, and one‑of‑a‑kind details are selected from curated palettes and materials libraries. Artisans translate your brief into hand sketches and digital renderings in real time, while Champagne and Alsatian canapés are served at the workstation. The appointment concludes with a comprehensive specification dossier and a scale model of the proposed car.

Name: The Hurlingham Club Private Tennis Lesson
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private tennis session on the riverside grounds of The Hurlingham Club in Fulham, set among grass and clay courts edged by formal gardens. A former professional player leads a personalised lesson, calibrating drills and point play to surface and ability, while a photographer documents the session from courtside.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Rolls-Royce Goodwood Commissioning Session
Master_Aurora_Insights: Inside the bespoke lounge at Rolls‑Royce’s Goodwood headquarters in West Sussex, you collaborate with the marque’s designers to personalise a Phantom, Cullinan or Spectre. Choices span hand‑picked wood veneers, leathers and commissioned embroidery, with artisans crafting digital and physical mock‑ups as the specification takes shape.

Name: Wimbledon Aorangi Practice Courts Private Coaching with Former Champion
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private coaching session on Wimbledon’s Aorangi practice courts, led by a former champion. The hit unfolds on the same grass surfaces where players train during The Championships at the All England Lawn Tennis Club, with a photographer courtside to document your serves and volleys. After play, you move to a private lounge for strawberries and cream, a Wimbledon tradition,  and leave with a signed memento.

Name: Mouratoglou Academy Private Tennis Session
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private court session at Patrick Mouratoglou’s academy on the Côte d’Azur, a training base created by the coach known for his work with Serena Williams. The experience begins with video-based analysis before moving onto a secluded court for targeted drills led by the academy staff. A professional photographer records your progress throughout, providing a visual record of the session.

Name: Andy Murray Tennis Coaching, Match, and Dinner
Master_Aurora_Insights: Trade serves and volleys with Andy Murray, three-time Grand Slam champion and former world No. 1, in an intimate match setting. A focused coaching session leads the day to refine your stroke and serve before you step on court. A professional film crew documents the experience on and off court and concludes with a post‑match dinner with Murray.

Name: La Quinta Padel Private Clinic with Pro
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private clinic at La Quinta Padel, an Andalusian club, led by a top‑ranked pro. You focus on strategy and shot selection on court. Between sets, the coach recounts stories from international tournaments. A photographer documents the play throughout.

Name: PBI World Private Tennis Lesson with Ex‑Pro
Master_Aurora_Insights: PBI World stages a private, location‑tailored court session through its global network of coaches and venues, available from Monaco to Miami. An ex‑pro leads focused work on strokes and footwork, tailored to where you play. A photographer documents improvement throughout.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Cancellations must be made at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled lesson time to avoid being charged the full lesson fee.

Name: Rafael Nadal One-on-One Tennis Match and Dinner
Master_Aurora_Insights: A one-on-one match with Rafael Nadal structured from warm‑up to debrief. The session opens on court with a warm‑up led by his personal coach, then moves into live play where you rally and trade points with the champion. A video crew records every shot for a post‑produced film. The program concludes with a private dinner with Nadal to review the match.

Name: Cliff Drysdale Tennis Private Coaching with Tour Professional
Master_Aurora_Insights: Cliff Drysdale Tennis hosts a private court session at one of its luxury resort locations. The clinic is tailored to your game and led by a tour‑experienced professional. An on‑court photographer documents the session.

Name: Matteo Berrettini Tennis Session and Dinner
Master_Aurora_Insights: An on‑court session with Matteo Berrettini, the Italian ATP Tour player and Wimbledon finalist. It begins with a warm‑up and tactical pointers from Berrettini, then you play a friendly yet competitive set, with cameras recording the play.

Name: Tommy Haas Tennis Coaching, Match, and Dinner
Master_Aurora_Insights: An afternoon on court with former ATP World No. 2 Tommy Haas. It opens with a personalised coaching session tuned to your game, then moves into a competitive set against Haas. A video crew documents the exchanges throughout. Dinner with Haas concludes the day.

Name: Roger Federer On-Court Rallies and Q&A
Master_Aurora_Insights: A charity match organised with the Roger Federer Foundation places you on court for rallies with Roger Federer, with participation supporting the foundation’s educational initiatives, which focus on quality education programs in Southern Africa and Switzerland. Federer’s stature as a 20-time Grand Slam singles champion frames the encounter, while a professional production team films the match throughout to document the session.

Name: Fernando Verdasco Tennis Match
Master_Aurora_Insights: A match-play session against Fernando Verdasco, the Spanish left-hander and former world No. 7 known for his powerful forehand. A private coach fine-tunes your game before you step on court, then you face Verdasco for a filmed encounter.

Name: Michael Jordan Invitational Match Play with Michael Jordan
Master_Aurora_Insights: Celebrity Match Play at the Michael Jordan Invitational places you inside a tournament round alongside Michael Jordan. The format is match play, with a professional caddie on your bag to set strategy and manage the course. The day concludes with an awards dinner that includes photos and autographs with Jordan.

Name: Gareth Bale Match Play Golf and Clubhouse Dinner
Master_Aurora_Insights: A round of match play golf with Gareth Bale, the football legend now directing his competitive drive toward fairways and greens. A golf professional offers swing tips before you tee off alongside Bale. Videography documents the day on course, from the first tee through the final putt.

Name: Sergio García Match Play Round and Clinic
Master_Aurora_Insights: Match play on course with Masters champion and Ryder Cup standout Sergio García. A focused warm‑up clinic addresses your swing mechanics before you tee off together.

Name: Augusta National Golf Club Round
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private day of golf at Augusta National Golf Club, home of the Masters Tournament in Augusta, Georgia. You walk the fairways on a day ordinarily reserved for members and past champions, with a resident caddie guiding you through Amen Corner (holes 11–13) and the club’s greens. A PGA professional offers on-course insight and practical tips.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: St Andrews Old Course Guaranteed Tee Time with Caddie
Master_Aurora_Insights: A guaranteed tee time on the Old Course at St Andrews, organized well in advance. The day opens on the practice range before you step onto the first tee, joined by an experienced caddie while a professional guide narrates the history underfoot. Between holes, the clubhouse serves Scottish fare. Post-round, a PGA coach delivers analysis of your play.

Name: Wentworth Club West Course Playing Lesson
Master_Aurora_Insights: A coached round at Wentworth Club in Surrey on the West Course, the Harry Colt–designed heathland layout that stages the BMW PGA Championship. A club professional opens with a pre‑round clinic to tune your swing, then accompanies you on course. Guidance continues as you navigate heather‑lined fairways and fast greens. After the round, the professional delivers a tailored lesson review.

Name: Monte-Carlo Golf Club Clinic and Round with Forecaddie
Master_Aurora_Insights: A day at Monte‑Carlo Golf Club set high above the Riviera with panoramic sea views and mountain air. The experience opens with a clinic led by a PGA professional before you head to the tee. A caddie accompanies you across a sequence of challenging holes, with the Mediterranean in sight throughout play.

Name: Terre Blanche Golf Clinic, PGA Pro Round, and Spa
Master_Aurora_Insights: Set in Provence’s rolling countryside, Terre Blanche offers two championship courses and a luxury spa. The day is coordinated in advance: you begin with a clinic at the Albatros Golf Performance Center, then play a round with a PGA professional. A gourmet lunch is served on a terrace overlooking the olive groves, and access to the spa completes the itinerary.

Name: Tiger Woods Golf Clinic, Round, and Lunch
Master_Aurora_Insights: A round of golf with Tiger Woods begins with a brief clinic. He fine-tunes your swing and course strategy, then steps onto the tee for play, with instruction continuing on course alongside friendly competition. Cameras document the round and after the final putt, a private lunch with Woods, who shares stories from his career as a 15-time major champion.

Name: Les Bordes Loire Valley Golf Round with PGA Professional
Master_Aurora_Insights: Access to the private Les Bordes estate in France’s Loire Valley for a guided round with a PGA professional. You warm up on the driving range, then play 18 holes routed through pine forests and wetlands characteristic of the Sologne. The estate is known for courses by Robert von Hagge and Gil Hanse, set across quiet woodland and water features that define the landscape.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: FC Bayern München Matchday Hospitality with Player Meet-and-Greet
Master_Aurora_Insights: A matchday at Allianz Arena in Munich, watching FC Bayern München from premium seating with gourmet dining and attentive service. The game unfolds with hospitality at your seat, then continues post‑match with a meet‑and‑greet for autographs and photos with players. A signed Bayern kit is included to take home.

Please understand that, as a general rule, tickets cannot be returned.

The exchange and return of tickets is generally prohibited. Tickets maintain their validity in case of a venue or date change. In such cases, the booking can be cancelled by the customer, if they are not able - or do not wish - to attend the match. The cancellation must be communicated either in writing (including via email), via the Digital Ticket Center, by fax, or by mail correspondence. The customer will be reimbursed the face value of the ticket, once the ticket has been presented or returned to FCB via post at the customer's own expense. Additional costs, such as administrative and shipping fees, are non-refundable.

In the event of cancellation of the event or at an event which, according to the requirements of a competent association or a competent authority, must take place completely or partially with the exclusion of spectators, FCB is entitled to withdraw from the contract for the purchase of one or more tickets for the affected event. In this case, the customer will be reimbursed the ticket price paid only upon presentation of the original ticket.

Name: Ferrari F1 Maranello Factory Tour and Simulator
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Access Ferrari’s Formula 1 headquarters in Maranello for an inside view of how race cars are designed and assembled. The visit moves from the factory floor to the wind tunnel, then into a simulator session normally reserved for drivers. Over lunch with engineers, you discuss race strategy and car development in practical terms. 

Comparable access can be arranged with McLaren, Mercedes‑AMG, and Red Bull Racing, with non‑disclosure agreements and schedules coordinated to protect active programs.

Name: Vacheron Constantin Watchmaking Masterclass
Master_Aurora_Insights: A watchmaking masterclass with Vacheron Constantin artisans, held in a luminous workshop. Participants assemble parts of a mechanical movement, feeling how wheels, plates, and springs align and interact. Master watchmakers explain the Geneva Seal alongside the maison’s history dating to 1755, and demonstrate why finishing and decoration matter as much as mechanics.

Name: Patek Philippe Geneva Salon Watchmaking Workshop
Master_Aurora_Insights: Inside Patek Philippe’s Geneva salon, a hands-on watchmaking session focuses on the construction of a manually wound calibre. Seated at a watchmaker’s bench, you assemble components using loupes and specialised tools under the guidance of Patek Philippe instructors. Instruction is interwoven with stories of the maison’s family ownership, the logic of perpetual calendars, and the hand‑finishing of bridges and screws.

Name: A. Lange & Söhne Glashütte Watchmaking Workshop
Master_Aurora_Insights: Inside A. Lange & Söhne’s ateliers in the Saxon town of Glashütte, you take a seat at a watchmaker’s bench to assemble the components of a German movement defined by the Glashütte three‑quarter plate and a hand‑engraved balance cock. A master watchmaker guides each step and outlines the manufactory’s post‑reunification revival, the rationale behind its signature outsize date, and how precision and finish are pursued across the calibres. Midway, a lunch of regional Saxon specialities opens a conversation on the distinctions between German and Swiss horology, architecture of the plate, finishing approaches, and functional priorities.

Name: F.P. Journe Movement Assembly Workshop
Master_Aurora_Insights: Inside F.P. Journe’s atelier, the brand’s watchmakers lead an intimate, hands-on session in independent horology. You assemble a mechanical movement from first components to its first tick, with instruction on resonance, remontoirs d’égalité, and the pursuit of chronometric precision. Conversations at the bench open François‑Paul Journe’s philosophy of authenticity and invention, grounding the techniques in the brand’s approach to craft.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: MB&F Geneva Horological Machine Assembly Workshop
Master_Aurora_Insights: A hands-on workshop inside MB&F’s Geneva lab led by the brand’s horological engineers. Participants deconstruct and reassemble elements of a kinetic sculpture, MB&F’s “Horological Machine”, using the bench as a place to examine how art and mechanics are engineered into working timepieces. The team shares first-hand stories of collaborations with artists and the practical challenges of making unconventional forms function with reliability.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Greubel Forsey Watchmaking Masterclass
Master_Aurora_Insights: A hands-on watchmaking masterclass inside Greubel Forsey’s secluded atelier. Guided by a specialist, you assemble components of a movement that may include inclined tourbillons and 30-degree escapements, seeing why tolerances measured in microns determine performance. You handle hand-frosted bridges and study the finishing techniques that define the brand’s aesthetic and mechanical standards.

Name: Jaeger-LeCoultre Manufacture Watchmaking Workshop and Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: Inside Jaeger-LeCoultre’s Manufacture in Le Sentier, in the Vallée de Joux, this workshop situates you at a bench to assemble a calibre under the guidance of working watchmakers. The visit moves through the integrated factory home to creations including the Reverso and the Atmos clock while experts explain how hundreds of components are produced in-house.

Name: Breguet Watchmaking Workshop
Master_Aurora_Insights: A hands-on watchmaking workshop with Breguet that opens the maison’s historic world, shaped since the era of Marie Antoinette. At a watchmaker’s bench, you assemble parts of a movement under expert supervision, gaining practical insight into inventions such as the tourbillon and the Breguet hands. The maison’s historians recount stories of Abraham‑Louis Breguet’s clientele as you work, linking the bench practice to centuries of horological achievement.

Name: De Bethune Watch Movement Assembly Workshop
Master_Aurora_Insights: Inside De Bethune’s modern Swiss workshop, you work alongside master watchmakers to assemble a contemporary calibre that uses high‑tech materials such as silicon and titanium. The session examines how traditional movement architecture is reinterpreted for performance. The team shares the brand’s philosophy of simplicity, balance and cosmic inspiration, and invites handling of polished, star‑studded dials and mirror‑finished components.

Name: Audemars Piguet Watchmaking Workshop in Le Brassus
Master_Aurora_Insights: A hands-on watchmaking workshop with Audemars Piguet in Le Brassus, in the heart of Switzerland’s Vallée de Joux. Guided by the Manufacture’s master watchmakers, you assemble and regulate a mechanical movement while learning how gears, springs, and jewels interact to measure time. Bench sessions introduce finishing techniques and trace the house’s history, from the Royal Oak to minute repeaters.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: The Ticket holder may cancel – and request reimbursement for – the guided tour or reserved activity by contacting the MAAP at least seven working days before the date indicated on the Ticket. Beyond this time limit, no reimbursement will be made. If applicable, a reimbursement of the total Ticket price will be credited to the payment or credit card account that was used for the purchase of the cancelled Ticket, to the exclusion of all other means of reimbursement.

Name: Patek Philippe Geneva Museum and Manufacture Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: An inside visit to Patek Philippe’s Geneva headquarters combining collection, craft, and conversation. A guided tour of the museum moves through historic pocket watches and complications, including the Henry Graves Supercomplication, before you step into the manufacture to observe the watchmaking floor. In the workshops, artisans hand‑polish movement bridges and set precious stones at the bench. The itinerary includes an introduction to the Rare Handcrafts department, where cloisonné enamel and marquetry are demonstrated in situ. Lunch with a senior executive opens a dialogue about commissioning a one‑of‑a‑kind timepiece, with model presentations tailored to your interests.

Name: Vacheron Constantin Manufacture and Atelier Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: Inside Vacheron Constantin’s modern manufacture in Plan‑les‑Ouates, Geneva, a historian leads an immersion in 260 years of watchmaking before opening the doors to working ateliers. At the benches, artisans hand‑engrave dials and assemble ultra‑thin movements under the loupe. Archival pieces come out for close study, alongside an introduction to Les Cabinotiers, the maison’s bespoke department. A private lunch with a master watchmaker allows direct conversation on complications and finishing. The models presented and the level of atelier access are customised to your interests and the maison’s availability.

Name: François‑Paul Journe Geneva Atelier Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: In Geneva, François‑Paul Journe opens his atelier to share the philosophy behind his chronometer‑grade timepieces in a guided look at how they are made. The tour follows each movement from raw material to finished watch, built entirely in‑house. At the benches, you observe watchmakers adjust remontoir d’égalité constant‑force mechanisms and hand‑finish bridges, tracking components through finishing and assembly.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: A. Lange & Söhne Glashütte Watch Manufacture Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: A watch manufacture visit inside A. Lange & Söhne in Glashütte, Saxony, Germany’s watchmaking center. The itinerary moves through historic buildings and contemporary workshops, where watchmakers work under magnification to engrave balance cocks and assemble three‑quarter plates. You continue into the academy, observing how apprentices hone their craft at training benches, then into the museum to view heritage pieces that chart the maison’s technical and aesthetic evolution.

Name: Richard Mille Les Breuleux Atelier Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: A behind-the-scenes visit to Richard Mille’s atelier in Les Breuleux, in the Swiss Jura. The tour opens with a technical presentation on the brand’s use of carbon TPT and titanium, then moves into the workshops where watchmakers assemble complex movements designed to withstand extreme G‑forces.

Name: Greubel Forsey La Chaux-de-Fonds Manufacture Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: A guided visit inside Greubel Forsey’s manufacture in La Chaux‑de‑Fonds, a Swiss watchmaking center. The tour moves through the workshop where hand‑finishing and inventive complications define the house’s ethos. At the benches, you observe watchmakers polish tourbillon bridges to a mirror finish and assemble inclined escapements. A presentation outlines the philosophy of time as sculpture and explains the Double Tourbillon 30°. Lunch is held in the horological farmstead with a brand representative, opening a conversation on the future of independent watchmaking. The complexity of the pieces shown and the level of technical detail are calibrated to your interest.

Name: De Bethune L'Auberson Atelier Private Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private visit to De Bethune’s atelier in L’Auberson, in Switzerland’s Jura, where a small team builds astronomy‑inspired wristwatches. The tour moves through case‑making and finishing: blued‑titanium cases being hand‑polished, the brand’s delta‑shaped bridges assembled at the bench, and Microlight surface technologies tested under magnification.

Name: Audemars Piguet Le Brassus Museum and Atelier Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: Audemars Piguet opens its Le Brassus headquarters in Switzerland’s Vallée de Joux for a private immersion in haute horlogerie. An archivist introduces the brand’s heritage museum before you enter the atelier where watchmakers assemble Royal Oak movements under microscopes. You handle components, observe finishing techniques at the bench, and view rare complications from the manufacture.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: The Ticket holder may cancel – and request reimbursement for – the guided tour or reserved activity by contacting the MAAP at least seven working days before the date indicated on the Ticket. Beyond this time limit, no reimbursement will be made. Name: De Bethune Private Watch Commission
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private commission with De Bethune at the brand’s Swiss atelier, known for cosmic blue titanium and modern interpretations of classical watchmaking. The process begins with a dialogue on motifs star‑studded skies, spherical moon phases, architectural lugs and the movement you want to power them. You review working prototypes as the piece develops, with the option to adjust dial layout or case size before finalization.

Name: Greubel Forsey Watch Commission
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private commission with Greubel Forsey centered on high horology. The process begins in La Chaux‑de‑Fonds, where founders Robert Greubel and Stephen Forsey guide an immersion into the maison’s patented tourbillons and inclined escapements. Together you determine the regulating mechanisms, from quadruple tourbillons to inclined double escapements, and select case metals and finishing styles.

Name: F.P. Journe Custom Watch Commission in Geneva
Master_Aurora_Insights: A bespoke commission with F.P. Journe begins in Geneva with a personal meeting with François‑Paul Journe to define complications, case size, and materials. His atelier then develops a unique calibre or adapts an existing movement to the brief.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Pace Gallery After-Hours Curator-Led Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: An after-hours tour of Pace Gallery led by a curator. Founded in New York in the 1960s, Pace has long championed major artists of the last century. The visit begins at a closed door, a key turning, and a glass of Champagne in hand before a guided walk through installations and paintings that span movements from kinetic light works to monumental abstracts.

Name: White Cube After-Hours Gallery Tour with Curator
Master_Aurora_Insights: After-hours access to White Cube with a curator-led walk through the current exhibitions. The doors are closed to the public, leaving the gallery’s stark, high‑ceilinged rooms quiet and unhurried. A curator greets you on arrival and guides you between installations, Champagne in hand, opening a focused conversation on the artists’ ideas, materials, and process.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Thaddaeus Ropac Gallery After-Hours Curator Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private, after-hours tour at Thaddaeus Ropac led by a curator. You arrive after closing and are welcomed with a glass of Champagne before moving through salons hung with work by major contemporary artists. The galleries are known for museum‑quality exhibitions staged in spaces that feel both grand and inviting; in the quiet, the curator details how each canvas and sculpture was conceived, and the gallery’s role in the global art community. Conversation ranges from Viennese expressionism to new media as you stroll without interruption. Discreet acquisition support is available if a work interests you
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Opera Gallery After-Hours Curator-Led Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private after-hours tour inside Opera Gallery led by a curator. Champagne in hand, you move through rooms where Impressionist paintings may hang beside contemporary sculpture. Conversation focuses on artists’ trajectories, the gallery’s relationships with ateliers and estates, and the shifting dynamics of the market.

Name: David Zwirner After-Hours Curator-Led Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: After the gallery closes, a senior curator greets you with a toast and leads a private tour through David Zwirner’s exhibition spaces. The route moves across current shows in painting, sculpture, video, and installation. The curator explains how each exhibition took shape, draws out relationships between works, and relays artists’ narratives from the gallery’s program.

Name: Marian Goodman Gallery Curator-Led After-Hours Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: An after-hours visit to Marian Goodman Gallery led by a curator. You are welcomed quietly, served Champagne, and guided through the current exhibitions. The conversation centers on the gallery’s long-term collaborations with its artists, the context of individual works, and the gallery’s influence on global collecting.

Name: Almine Rech After-Hours Curator-Led Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: An after-hours tour inside Almine Rech, led by a curator. Outside public hours, you are greeted with Champagne before moving through light‑filled rooms. The visit focuses on works ranging from figuration to abstraction and points where avant‑garde practice meets tradition, with attention to why each placement is made. Along the way, the curator shares how certain artists were discovered, explains studio processes, and outlines the gallery’s aesthetic philosophy.

Name: Hermès Leather Accessory Workshop
Master_Aurora_Insights: A bespoke workshop inside Hermès’ petite ateliers brings you into close work with the maison’s saddlers and leather artisans. The session covers core techniques, hand-stitching, dyeing, and finishing, applied to an accessory you design: a Kelly‑inspired handbag, a watch strap, or a belt. You select colours, linings, and hardware while working amid rolls of Barénia leather and stacks of silk scarves. A master craftsman guides the process, teaching the saddle‑stitch with two needles and waxed linen thread at a deliberate pace.

Name: Creative Workshop at Loro Piana
Master_Aurora_Insights: A creative workshop inside Loro Piana’s workrooms. It begins with a tactile study of cashmere and vicuña fibres, then moves to sketching and selecting patterns for a coat, cardigan, or travel set. Skilled seamstresses demonstrate cutting and hand‑sewing techniques and invite you to place a stitch. Your finished piece arrives weeks later, labelled with your initials and accompanied by a certificate.

Name: Dior Maison Porcelain and Crystal Design Workshop
Master_Aurora_Insights: Dior Maison hosts a creative workshop in a Parisian salon focused on designing porcelain or crystal pieces for the table and home. You meet with the creative team to select shapes, motifs and colour palettes drawn from Monsieur Dior’s gardens or the house’s toile de Jouy. Artisans demonstrate hand‑painting and gilding techniques, then invite you to add brushstrokes or initial your piece.

Name: Brunello Cucinelli Solomeo Tailoring and Knitwear Workshop
Master_Aurora_Insights: A hands-on design session inside Brunello Cucinelli’s Solomeo headquarters in Umbria. The day begins with a walk through the castle‑turned‑atelier, where the team outlines the house’s approach to humanistic capitalism, ethical sourcing, and craftsmanship. Guided by master tailors and knitters, you design a cashmere sweater or an unstructured jacket, selecting yarns, stitches, and colors. You may step onto the workroom floor to finish a seam or weave a label.

Name: Piaget Geneva Watchmaking and High Jewelry Workshop
Master_Aurora_Insights: A hands-on design session inside Piaget’s Geneva atelier that brings watchmaking and high jewellery into the same workflow. The maison, known for ultra‑thin movements, invites consultation with its designers on the case shape, dial colour, and gem setting of a timepiece or jewel. Watchmakers explain how movements are assembled, while gem‑setters demonstrate micro‑pavé techniques.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Gagosian After-Hours Curator-Led Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: An after-hours walkthrough of Gagosian led by a senior curator, and, depending on availability, the exhibiting artist. The galleries are closed to the public, allowing an unhurried circuit through rooms of contemporary painting and sculpture. The conversation centers on the works at hand: materials, process, and context, with pauses to examine pieces at close range.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: P3 Applied Sports Science Santa Barbara Training Residency
Master_Aurora_Insights:
A precision training residency at P3 Applied Sports Science in Santa Barbara, used by elite athletes and Olympians. You move through biomechanical motion capture and metabolic testing to establish baselines before a personalized program is built, combining neuromuscular training with targeted recovery protocols. Sessions run with real-time data analysis to adjust load and mechanics, supported by cryo and compression recovery and nutrition calibration aimed at measurable performance improvement. 

Aurora Edge adds a private intake slot with the head coach, a video-recorded performance breakdown, and a take-home plan laid out after training.

Name: Human Performance Reset – Clinique La Prairie (Montreux, Switzerland)
Master_Aurora_Insights:
A data-driven longevity retreat at Clinique La Prairie in Montreux, Switzerland, on Lake Geneva. Genomic testing and cellular-level diagnostics inform tailored protocols across nutrition, movement, and recovery. Physician-led consultations structure the stay; treatments include personalized IV infusions and hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Biomarkers are tracked over time through concierge follow-ups after departure. 

For Aurora members: preferential booking windows, complimentary lab follow-up, and a wellness progress review at 30 days.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: A deposit of 50% of the total amount is required to confirm the booking. Cancellations made more than 30 days prior to arrival will receive a full refund. Cancellations made within 30 days of arrival will forfeit the deposit.

Name: The Altitude Adaptation Residency – Flagstaff Performance Institute (Arizona)
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Set at 7,000 ft inside Flagstaff’s endurance-training corridor, the residency at Flagstaff Performance Institute pairs morning endurance blocks with clinical recovery. Designed by former Olympic physiologists, the program targets altitude adaptation with measurable outcomes for founders and athletes looking to reset cardiovascular and cellular efficiency. Flagstaff’s high plateau has long served distance runners and cyclists, providing consistent elevation for aerobic conditioning. 

Aurora Edge adds priority access to the head physiologist, a personalized recovery report, and a continued oxygen‑training plan post‑residency.

Name: Othership x Aurora Contrast Therapy and Breathwork Circuit
Master_Aurora_Insights:
A guided heat–cold performance ritual by Othership x Aurora, combining ice immersion, guided breathwork, and thermal oscillation for rapid cellular recovery. Structured as a circuit, the session moves between heat and ice while breathwork anchors the transitions. Sessions measure progress: thermal adaptation and breath efficiency are tracked over time, making contrast therapy a measurable resilience practice. 

The Aurora Edge covers private group bookings, a recovery‑breath data report, and follow‑up digital integration.

Name: After-Hours Museum Preview at Fondation Louis Vuitton
Master_Aurora_Insights: After the Fondation Louis Vuitton closes to the public, a private, guided preview moves through its glass-and-timber interior. The Frank Gehry designed museum in the Bois de Boulogne is presented through its ever changing exhibitions and works from the contemporary collection, with clear context on artistic innovation and the building’s architecture.

In accordance with the provisions of Article L. 221-28, 12° of the French Consumer Code, Purchasers are not entitled to cancel an Order. Tickets cannot be returned, refunded (including in case of the loss or theft of tickets), exchanged, or resold. In case of cancellation of an event by the Foundation, the face value of the ticket paid by the Purchaser to the Foundation shall be refunded.

Name: After-Hours Gallery Preview at Tate Modern
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private after-hours preview inside Tate Modern, London’s museum of international modern and contemporary art on Bankside. As the Turbine Hall dims and the escalators fall silent, a dedicated curator leads your group through the building’s industrial volumes, part of the former Bankside Power Station, reimagined by Herzog & de Meuron, to view major installations and rotating exhibitions without crowds. The tour weaves clear context about artists and their methods, with time to stand before works by Mark Rothko or Anish Kapoor and register their scale without hurry.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Tickets are non-refundable and non-exchangeable. However, providing we have availability, we may be able to exchange some exhibition tickets at our discretion, for a different date or time, subject to availability and provided you return the unwanted ticket before their valid date and time slot.
Fulfillment Steps: Lead 4–8 weeks; varies by institution, exhibition scale and curator level.

Name: Centre Pompidou After-Hours Tour with Curator
Master_Aurora_Insights: An after-hours tour of the Centre Pompidou led by a curator versed in postwar art. The visit moves through quiet galleries and architectural vantage points inside the museum’s high-tech structure by Renzo Piano and Richard Rogers, with context on the centre’s avant-garde collections. Light refreshments are served as the group lingers by works such as Kandinsky’s abstractions and Duchamp’s provocations, with time for questions and conversation rarely possible during public hours. The pace is unhurried, alternating between art viewing and moments that frame the building’s exposed steel and glass, including its signature external escalators. The evening concludes on the rooftop terraces with panoramic views across Paris.
Fulfillment Steps: Lead 4–8 weeks; varies by institution, exhibition scale and curator level.

Name: Galleria Borghese After-Hours Private Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private, after-hours preview inside the Galleria Borghese, the Roman villa set within the Borghese gardens. Once the museum closes, your group enters empty marble halls for a guided circuit led by a specialist art historian. Rooms hung with works by Caravaggio and Bernini are approached at a measured pace, with context on Cardinal Scipione Borghese, the collector who assembled the core holdings. Between galleries, you pause in a salon for Prosecco and Italian hors d’oeuvres. Freed from daytime crowds, you can linger before Bernini’s Apollo and Daphne and Caravaggio’s David with the Head of Goliath. Frescoes register cleanly under evening lighting, and the route is shaped to your interests within the baroque interiors. The museum remains closed to the public as a final stop is taken in front of a marble group in a silent, unoccupied room.

Cancellations made between 29 days and 48 hours prior to the tour date are eligible for a 50% refund or 50% future travel credit, less any ticket, reservation, and/or applicable service fees. All sales are final within 48 hours of the tour date. Venue tickets and reservation fees are non refundable and non transferable and cannot be used without a Context tour.
Fulfillment Steps: Lead 4–8 weeks; varies by institution, exhibition scale and curator level.

Name: Uffizi After-Hours Private Tour with Art Historian
Master_Aurora_Insights: After the Uffizi closes, a discreet entrance opens and you step inside for a private preview led by a Florentine art historian. The visit moves through the galleries in chronological sequence, pausing before Botticelli’s Primavera, Leonardo da Vinci’s Annunciation, and Michelangelo’s Doni Tondo. Without daytime crowds, there is time to study details and ask questions in an unhurried exchange with the guide. Between rooms, the group retreats to a loggia for aperitivi and light bites with views over the Arno.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Cancellations must be made in writing to booking@artviva.com. All services are non-refundable except for Semi Private Tours where the cancelation is made before 7 days ahead of the tour. In case of no-show or cancellation before the service, no refund will be provided. We will not be responsible for partial shows during the tour including leaving early on a service.
Fulfillment Steps: Lead 4–8 weeks; varies by institution, exhibition scale and curator level.

Name: After-Hours Museum Preview at Guggenheim Bilbao
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private after-hours preview inside the Guggenheim Bilbao, Frank Gehry’s titanium-clad museum on the Nervión. After closing time, a museum docent leads an unhurried walk through galleries of contemporary art and site-specific installations, with attention to how the works sit within the architecture. Tapas and Txakoli are served in a lounge between exhibition spaces.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND
Fulfillment Steps: Lead 4–8 weeks; varies by institution, exhibition scale and curator level.

Name: Musée d’Orsay Private After-Hours Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: A private after-hours visit to the Musée d’Orsay, entered once the public has left and the station clocks mark the moment. A specialist leads a tailored circuit through the museum’s galleries of Impressionism and Symbolism, pausing with works by Monet, Degas, and Gauguin so you can study the canvases without crowds. Light refreshments are served on a mezzanine overlooking the Seine. Freed from daytime flow, the pace is unhurried: linger under the Beaux‑Arts station’s great iron arches and take time with details across nineteenth‑century painting and the building’s architecture.
Fulfillment Steps: Lead 4–8 weeks; varies by institution, exhibition scale and curator level.

Name: Fondazione Prada After-Hours Curator-Led Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: After closing time at Fondazione Prada, you enter its OMA/Rem Koolhaas–designed art campus in south Milan for a private, after-hours preview. A curator leads a customized evening walk through changing exhibitions and permanent installations, linking contemporary works to wider cultural narratives and to the site’s architecture, including the tower that anchors the former distillery complex. Between spaces, you pause in a private lounge for a glass of Franciacorta and small plates, a moment to compare impressions before reentering the galleries.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Booking is mandatory and must be requested at least 7 days prior to the visit date. If the visit should not be possible on the day booked, the ticket will not be refunded or cancelled.
Fulfillment Steps: Lead 4–8 weeks; varies by institution, exhibition scale and curator level.

Name: Christie’s Auction Preview and Bidding Consultation
Master_Aurora_Insights: Christie’s opens its private viewing rooms for a pre-sale preview with optional bidding rights. Before the saleroom lights come up and the gavel falls, you review forthcoming lots behind closed doors alongside a specialist in your collecting field. Paintings, jewels, and watches are handled under white gloves while you hear notes on provenance and market trends. A curator sets the sale in context over Champagne, explaining distinctions such as Impressionist versus Modern painting and the craftsmanship of a rare watch. If you choose to bid, a dedicated concierge is available to discuss credit arrangements and strategy for participating in the auction.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND
Fulfillment Steps: Lead 6–10 weeks; dependent on auction house, sale category and bidding credit.

Name: National Gallery London After-Hours Curator-Led Tour
Master_Aurora_Insights: An after-hours preview inside the National Gallery, London. A senior curator leads you through galleries of Renaissance altarpieces and Romantic landscapes, drawing out details and provenance that go unremarked during daytime visits. With the museum closed, you can linger before Turner’s swirling seas and Velázquez’s portraits, setting the pace room by room. Midway, Champagne and canapés are served in a private space overlooking Trafalgar Square, a pause to discuss how the collection was assembled.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Any cancellation requests must be made via email to TravelTrade@nationalgallery.org.uk at least 14 working days prior to the date of your tour. Name: Core by Clare Smyth
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Notting Hill, this three-Michelin-starred venue is the debut solo restaurant from Clare Smyth, the first British female chef to hold the guide’s highest accolade.
The light-filled dining room emphasizes sustainable British produce and natural materials, presenting a modern interpretation of fine dining without white tablecloths.
A signature course elevates the humble potato with dulse beurre blanc and roe, reflecting the kitchen's commitment to celebrating modest ingredients.

Name: Dinner by Heston Blumenthal
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Housed within the Mandarin Oriental Hyde Park, this two-Michelin-starred dining room presents a modern evolution of historic British gastronomy.
The kitchen team mines the country’s culinary archives to reconstruct centuries-old recipes with contemporary precision.
A signature Meat Fruit disguises chicken liver parfait as a textured mandarin orange in a nod to medieval trickery.

Name: Hélène Darroze at The Connaught
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Hélène Darroze’s three-Michelin-starred outpost at The Connaught brings her French culinary philosophy to the heart of Mayfair.
Designed by Pierre Yovanovitch, the wood-paneled space offers a warm backdrop for seasonal tasting menus centered on hand-selected produce.
A meal here often concludes with the signature babà, soaked in your choice of vintage Armagnac from the Darroze family cellars.

Name: Sushi Tetsu
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Tucked away in Clerkenwell, this seven-seat counter is the domain of former Nobu chef Toru Takahashi and his wife Harumi.
The intimate setting is defined by a purist’s omakase menu that prioritizes traditional Edomae techniques over modern fusion.
Meals culminate in a display of exacting knife work, as Takahashi scores fatty tuna before searing it with a handheld blowtorch.

Name: Humble Chicken
Master_Aurora_Insights:
In Soho, chef Angelo Sato leads this intimate thirteen-seat counter, which has evolved from a yakitori bar into a two-Michelin-starred dining destination.
The tasting menu applies European precision to Japanese ingredients, presenting a theatrical omakase progression that explores texture and flavor beyond traditional grilling.
Service culminates in the titular donabe rice pot with crispy chicken leg, preceded by signatures like shokupan with liver pâté and fermented plum.

Name: Kitchen Table
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Tucked away in Fitzrovia, this two-Michelin-starred restaurant from chef James Knappett offers a counter-dining experience for just 19 guests.
The setting features a horseshoe-shaped counter where diners watch the chefs prepare a daily changing tasting menu of modern British dishes.
A defining detail is the minimalist menu format, where each of the twenty courses is focused on and named after a single seasonal ingredient.

Name: Endo at the Rotunda
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Perched atop the former BBC Television Centre, this Michelin-starred omakase counter is the flagship of third-generation sushi master Endo Kazutoshi.
The intimate experience unfolds as a theatrical sequence of Edomae-style sushi, served against a backdrop of panoramic London views and Kengo Kuma’s design.
A signature "Business Card" hand roll of crisp nori and tuna begins the ritual, presented over a 200-year-old Hinoki wood counter.

Name: KOL
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Helmed by chef Santiago Lastra, this Marylebone destination is the first Mexican restaurant in the UK to hold a Michelin star.
The kitchen translates the soul of Mexican cuisine through a British larder, replacing traditional imports with foraged and seasonal produce.
Interiors feature corn husk marquetry by artist Fernando Laposse, while the signature langoustine taco arrives with the head on the side for squeezing.

Name: Ikoyi
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Jeremy Chan and Iré Hassan-Odukale, this two-Michelin-starred restaurant occupies a ground-floor space at 180 Strand.
The kitchen pairs West African spices with hyper-seasonal British produce to create complex dishes that defy simple geographic categorization.
Interiors by David Thulstrup feature copper-clad walls and curved metal mesh, a tactile backdrop for the signature smoked jollof rice.

Name: Bône
Master_Aurora_Insights: Chef Nas Sharif runs this Hoxton dining room, prioritizing premium halal meats and a straightforward culinary philosophy. The kitchen presents a concise set menu that pairs main proteins like steak or salmon with unlimited fries and house sauces. Guests visit for the signature eight-hour slow-cooked short rib, served in a candlelit space that maintains a popular BYOB policy.

Name: Plates
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Helmed by Great British Menu champion Kirk Haworth and his sister Keeley, this Michelin-starred Shoreditch destination operates as both a plant-based restaurant and a creative food studio.
The kitchen delivers high-concept vegan gastronomy that blends traditional craft with modern innovation, focusing on organic produce and wild foraged ingredients.
Courses are presented on bespoke recycled ceramics designed in collaboration with award-winning potter Sue Pryke.

Name: Legado
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Helmed by acclaimed chef Nieves Barragán Mohacho, this contemporary Shoreditch destination celebrates the diverse, lesser-known regional cuisines of Spain.
True to its name, meaning 'legacy', the kitchen moves beyond familiar tapas to offer nose-to-tail dishes like suckling pig ears and crab rice.
The drinks menu features an all-Spanish wine list and signature 'Three-Sip Serves', a flight of mini-cocktails paying homage to specific regions.

Name: Osteria Angelina
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Tucked away in a secluded Shoreditch courtyard, this laid-back sibling to Dalston’s Angelina is the work of restaurateurs Joshua Owens-Baigler and Amar Takhar.
The kitchen pursues the group’s signature *itameshi* style, merging Italian culinary traditions with Japanese ingredients in a spacious, darkly chic setting.
A standout starter is the toasted Hokkaido milk bread served with burnt honey and miso butter, best enjoyed before exploring the list of low-intervention wines.

Name: Crisp Pizza
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Carl McCluskey, this cult-followed residency occupies the historic, wood-panelled interiors of The Marlborough Arms in Mayfair.
The kitchen delivers a distinctive take on New York-style pizza, producing large pies with a sturdy structure and a base that remains consistently thin and crackly.
Diners order the signature square "Grandma Pie" or spicy honey-topped pepperoni, enjoying the contrast of precision baking within a traditional British tavern atmosphere.

Name: The Clove Club
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Housed in the Grade II-listed Shoreditch Town Hall, this two-Michelin-starred destination is led by chef Isaac McHale.
The kitchen serves a sophisticated tasting menu of modern British cuisine within a relaxed, high-ceilinged dining room.
A signature snack of buttermilk fried chicken dusted with pine salt is presented on a bed of pine needles.

Name: Lagana
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Brought to Shoreditch by the Pachamama Group, this Greek-inspired restaurant takes its name from a traditional flatbread.
The menu focuses on Mediterranean small plates and charcoal-grilled meats served in a space defined by a lively, communal atmosphere.
Tables are lined with paper and crayons, inviting guests to sketch while enjoying the signature house bread and dips.

Name: Gymkhana
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Mayfair, this two-Michelin-starred destination from JKS Restaurants channels the atmosphere of elite colonial-era Indian social clubs.
The space evokes a bygone era with dark wood paneling and rattan-trimmed booths, setting the stage for refined Northern Indian cuisine.
A standout experience involves ordering the signature kid goat methi keema with pao or the wild muntjac biryani amidst the room’s sepia-toned nostalgia.

Name: The Ledbury
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Notting Hill, this three-Michelin-starred destination is led by Australian chef Brett Graham.
The kitchen prioritizes sustainability and provenance, crafting modern British dishes centered around wild game and ingredients grown on-site.
A dedicated in-house fungarium cultivates the mushrooms used in the signature warm truffle royale.

Name: Brutto
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by the late restaurateur Russell Norman, this Clerkenwell trattoria pays homage to the rustic dining rooms of Florence with a Michelin Bib Gourmand to its name.
The unpretentious dining room operates on a "brutto ma buono" ethos, pairing a soundtrack of loud music with a low-lit, convivial atmosphere.
Diners typically order the signature penne with vodka or a Florentine steak, served alongside the house’s staple five-pound Negronis.

Name: Chiltern Firehouse
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Housed in a Grade II-listed Victorian fire station in Marylebone, this restaurant is the work of hotelier André Balazs and chef Nuno Mendes.
Paris-based Studio KO designed the interiors, pairing a warm, brasserie-style layout with an open kitchen that anchors the bustling dining room.
The menu’s enduring signature is the crab doughnut, dusted with coral and served before a selection of wood-fired mains.

Name: Nina
Master_Aurora_Insights:
From the team behind Bottarga and Zephyr, this Marylebone restaurant replaces the group's original Pachamama site with a high-energy Mediterranean concept.
The subterranean space is defined by a clubby energy, with a central bar anchoring a warren of candlelit rooms and a high-spec sound system.
Finish with the boozy tiramisu al cucchiaio, a generous bowl designed to be scooped and shared among the table.

Name: The Devonshire
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Revived by publican Oisín Rogers, Flat Iron founder Charlie Carroll, and chef Ashley Palmer-Watts, this Soho venue blends a traditional pub with a dedicated restaurant.
The building houses a lively ground-floor bar and an upstairs dining room focused on wood-fired British cookery.
Menu highlights include creel-caught langoustines and beef butchered on-site, served alongside fresh soda bread and the team's signature Guinness.

Name: Brat
Master_Aurora_Insights: Located in Shoreditch, this Michelin-starred destination from chef Tomos Parry draws inspiration from the wood-fired cooking traditions of the Basque country. The open kitchen acts as the room's anchor, where seasonal ingredients are prepared over open charcoal grills within a wood-panelled space. Its namesake dish is a whole turbot slow-cooked directly on the coals, serving as the centerpiece of the daily changing menu.

Name: Mountain
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying a spacious Soho site, this wood-fired restaurant and wine bar is the latest project from Michelin-starred chef Tomos Parry.
The kitchen marries Welsh ingredients with Spanish simplicity, centering on open-fire cooking and a daily-changing selection of produce-driven plates.
A standout order is the whole lobster caldereta, a rich Menorcan stew served in a clay pot for the table to share.

Name: Cheval Blanc
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Anchored in the Samaritaine complex, this gastronomic venue is led by chef Arnaud Donckele, bringing his three-Michelin-star pedigree to the banks of the Seine.
The kitchen reverses traditional hierarchy, treating intricate, perfumer-like sauces as the menu’s centerpiece rather than a mere accompaniment.
Diners enjoy these signature "Absolutes" in a Peter Marino-designed dining room that frames sweeping views of the Pont Neuf.

Name: Epicure
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Housed within Le Bristol Paris, this three-Michelin-starred restaurant is led by chef Arnaud Faye.
The dining room features bay windows opening onto a manicured courtyard garden, providing a bright backdrop for the chef's contemporary gastronomy.
A signature dish is the macaroni stuffed with black truffle, artichoke, and foie gras, gratinated with parmesan.

Name: Chez l'Ami Louis
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Recently acquired by LVMH, this centenarian institution in the 3rd arrondissement stands as a preserved example of the classic Parisian bistro.
The wood-paneled dining room operates as a 1930s time capsule, where white-jacketed waiters serve a high-powered clientele in a space unchanged by modern trends.
A meal here invariably centers on the house specialty of roast chicken, finished in a wood-fired oven and served alongside a signature potato galette.

Name: Frenchie
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Helmed by Chef Gregory Marchand, who earned his nickname from Jamie Oliver, this Michelin-starred destination anchors the culinary revival of the Sentier district's Rue du Nil.
The intimate dining room defines modern bistronomy by pairing rustic exposed brick walls with a globally inspired approach to French fundamentals.
Guests commit to a seasonal carte blanche tasting menu that changes daily to reflect the freshest available market ingredients.

Name: Bistrot Paul Bert
Master_Aurora_Insights: Located in the 11th arrondissement, this quintessential bistro is the enduring project of restaurateur Bertrand Auboyneau. The lively dining room defines the genre with its mosaic floors, red banquettes, and chalkboard menus listing hearty, traditional standards. A meal here is incomplete without the legendary steak au poivre, served rare with frites, followed by a towering Paris-Brest.
